slice.question: Can Chrome's static CT-log-list publication mechanisms provide a zero-live-Tiger-endpoint freshness/integrity gate for the narrow static eligibility/status discovery from r221?

observed_claims: Chrome's CT log lists are updated daily.
Chrome signs log_list/all_logs_list to facilitate offline verification using a published public key.
Consumers are encouraged to cache recent versions because the lists have no SLA or availability guarantee.
Google publishes a new CT Log list every day containing a fresh log_list_timestamp.
Chrome enforces CT while the freshest stored list has log_list_timestamp within the past 70 days and the format is understood; after 70 days without an updated list CT enforcement is disabled.
sources.use: same-leaf official-policy cross-check because the inspected Log Lists page itself did not state log_list_timestamp semantics

slice.finding: A cached Chrome CT log-list artifact can carry three useful static primitives without opening a Tiger log endpoint: a daily publication cadence, a detached Chrome signature intended for offline verification with a published key, and a log_list_timestamp whose age Chrome itself uses as a bounded staleness signal. This supports a zero-live-endpoint gate for authenticity/staleness of the Chrome-recognized list used for static eligibility/status discovery. The single inspected Log Lists page did not itself define log_list_timestamp; that detail required the same publisher's CT Policy cross-check, so the stronger single-page-completeness hypothesis is false in this slice.
slice.scope_limit: Only static Chrome list publication cadence, signed-list integrity primitive, caching guidance, and Chrome's documented log_list_timestamp freshness/enforcement semantics. No cryptographic signature was executed; no current log_list.json artifact timestamp was fetched; no Tiger endpoint, tree head, submission, certificate-specific inclusion, or operational reachability was tested.
